methodology.measure: Actual current Rust implementations; operation counts asserted by native tests. Metrics inject a counted HardwareSample producer. Model tests create real minimal GGUF and model-directory fixtures. Catalog tests use real reqwest HTTP requests to an in-process loopback axum server.
methodology.scope: Counts describe these synthetic workloads, not wall-clock responsiveness, production GPU command duration, browser latency or battery life. No before/after native UI latency claim is made.
methodology.baseline: The archived phase 2 source was inspected for the uncached call paths. These new counted workloads were run against phase 3; baseline counts below are characterized from source, not reported as a separately instrumented benchmark.

safetyRegressions: slow hardware work leaves the async executor responsive
cancelled metrics caller retains the single blocking-worker guard
no hardware sampling without an observer
root changes discard an older filesystem scan before publication
same-size edits and corrupt/repaired GGUF replacements invalidate the header cache
legacy sidecar hashing/deletion and MLX/diffusers separation remain covered
cancelled catalog initializer can be replaced by another waiter
catalog success TTL and bounded LRU evictions
implementationLimits: Model refresh still walks the configured directories and stats model/sidecar files; only unchanged GGUF/PALW header and sidecar JSON parsing is skipped. The initial cold model scan remains.

MLX and diffusers directories are deliberately rescanned because their own directory mtime does not describe nested weight edits. The cache is in memory and follows the existing root/depth/filter semantics.

Metrics hardware snapshot TTL is 500 ms; generation atomics are read for every response. The existing GPU-specific 500 ms polling cache remains. 100-to-1 refers to complete HardwareMonitor sample calls, not a claim of 100 nvidia-smi subprocesses in the baseline.

Catalog successful searches are cached for 30 seconds with 64 entries; repository results for 60 seconds with 32 entries. A new endpoint/token Catalog instance has a fresh cache. Errors are shared only while callers overlap, not negatively cached.
Native checks ran on Linux. Real desktop/WebView paint and interaction latency were not measured.

baselineSourceCharacteristics.hardwareStartup: System::new_all followed by refresh_all refreshes every process twice although HardwareSnapshot only consumes CPU and memory facts.
baselineSourceCharacteristics.metrics: Each MetricsHub.sample called HardwareMonitor.sample synchronously inside the async task; only the nested GPU probes had a TTL.
baselineSourceCharacteristics.modelStore: Each refresh starts its own spawn_blocking full scan, rereads every model header and can publish after a roots change; these paths have no shared request generation or metadata cache.
baselineSourceCharacteristics.catalog: The HTTP client is already shared by AppState. Search and repository requests had no response or in-flight cache. The tree used a branch name even after metadata returned an immutable commit.

referenceCodeRead.application: One active task with one coalesced later task; per-key independent work.
Coalesce watcher updates, release obsolete tracked requests, and reuse shared observation.
Bound background work and keep unchanged watchers instead of recreating them.

subsequentCompatibilityChange.change: Replace newly deprecated fetch_update with an equivalent compare_exchange_weak/saturating_sub loop; preserve Relaxed ordering and the existing underflow regression test.
subsequentCompatibilityChange.reason: Keep the Rust 1.88 minimum version while allowing Rust 1.100 clippy -D warnings.
subsequentCompatibilityChange.validation: rustfmt --check passed. Root owns the final full native test/clippy gate after this small compatibility change. sourceSha256.phase3 records the earlier targeted-test source.
